= =====================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 11 10-01-2025 1.
Heard Mr. Dhramveer, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr. Suresh Prasad Singh, learned APP for the State.

2. The instant petition has been filed for quashing the order dated 19.09.2011 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Patna, in Cr. Revision No. 292 of 2011 whereby the revision has been dismissed and the order dated 03.03.2011 passed by the learned S.D.J.M., Danapur, in connection with Danapur P.S. Case No. 29 of 2010 by which cognizance of the offences under Sections 467, 468, 420, 365,
366, 342, 120(B) of the Indian Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.40006 of 2016(11) dt.10-01-2025 Penal Code (in short 'IPC') has been affirmed.

3. The main grounds taken by the learned counsel for the petitioners to assail the order impugned are that the F.I.R. which has been lodged by the father of the victim, itself goes to show that at the time of alleged occurrence, the informant's daughter, so-called victim, was a student of graduation Saroj Kumar And Ors vs The State Of Bihar on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179835247/
1 course and it was accepted that there was family relationship between the accused/petitioners and informant's family and the allegations levelled by the informant in the F.I.R. are totally false and during investigation, the police found out the love affair being in between the informant's daughter and petitioner no.1 who later on solemnized marriage and mainly considering that aspect, the police submitted final form in favour of the petitioners but thereafter the learned Magistrate, while differing with the conclusion of the police, took cognizance of the alleged offences but no reason was given by the Magistrate in his order impugned and the said order was passed mechanically and thereafter, the petitioners challenged the said order before the revisional court where also the merit of the allegations was not examined, in fact, on account of the love affair between the petitioner no.1 and informant's daughter, they entered into marital relationship by performing marriage before Special Marriage Officer on 14.12.2006 and in this regard, Annexure-2 is Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.40006 of 2016(11) dt.10-01-2025 relevant and during investigation, the informant's daughter did not say anything in support of the allegation before the Judicial Magistrate and today in the light of the order dated 02.12.2024, the petitioner no.1 is present with the informant's daughter before this Court and they have been blessed with a daughter who is presently six years old.
4.

sentences.text:
Though, learned APP for the State has opposed this petition but fairly accepted that in the present time, there is marital relationship between the petitioner no.1 and the informant's daughter who is said to be the victim and in view of this relationship, a lenient approach may be taken.
5. Considering the above submissions and mainly taking into account the facts that in the F.I.R., the informant did not disclose the age of his daughter who is said to be the victim and as per the FIR at the time of alleged occurrence, the informant's daughter was a student of graduation course and during the investigation, she appeared before the Judicial Magistrate and did not support the allegations of the FIR as stated above rather accepted her marital relationship with the petitioner no.1 and considering that aspect the police submitted final form in favour of the petitioners and the learned Magistrate while differing with the conclusion of the police, did not assign any reason in the cognizance order which shows that the said Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.40006 of 2016(11)
dt.10-01-2025 order was passed in mechanical manner and the revisional court also did not mention any ground while dismissing the revision petition of the petitioners which also shows the mechanical approach by the revisional court and today the informant's daughter is present before this Court and she has accepted her marital relationship with petitioner no.1 since 2006 as well as one daughter having been blessed due to the conjugal relationship with the petitioner no.1 before this Court and in support of these facts she has filed her supplementary affidavit and also accepted her residing in his company since the year of marriage, in my opinion, in view of these facts, putting the petitioners for trial for the alleged offences would be complete harassment to them and also would not serve the ends of justice and further the impugned order as well as cognizance order were passed in a mechanical manner, so, both the said orders are hereby set aside and the instant Criminal Miscellaneous petition is allowed.
(Shailendra Singh, J) Amandeep/-
